{{Quote|Hang on, son! We'll move into the asteroid field. And we'll have a couple of surprises for him.|Jango Fett|<ref name="Episode 2">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
The '''Void-7''' was a type of [[Seismic charge/Legends|seismic charge]] that was manufactured and marketed by the [[Krupx Munitions/Legends|Krupx Munitions]] corporation, and was considered to be the height of "seismic" weapon technology as of the years surrounding the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Description==
{{Quote|They're rather useful for taking care of large groups of enemies.|[[TC-38]]|<ref name="Kinect Star Wars">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>}}
[[File:SeismicCharge-SWX.png|thumb|left|250px|A Void-7 seismic charge.]]
[[Krupx Munitions/Legends|Krupx Munitions]]' Void-7 [[Seismic charge/Legends|seismic charge]] comprised a large, rounded canister containing a mix of unstable liquid [[Baradium/Legends|baradium]] and volatile [[collapsium]] gas. This mix became supercharged by two electromagnetic exciter disks on either end of the weapon's core. Once released into space, these disks would infuse the core with energized impulses to excite the blended explosives.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The Void-7's explosion was characterized by a powerful implosion followed by a planar expanding energy wave of massive power, enough to decimate large [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]], like in the rings surrounding [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]]. Only the [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]] on a capital ship could protect against a Void-7 shock wave. The resulting explosion also temporarily canceled out sound before the shockwave released a loud humming sound. The explosive mix within a Void-7 could be altered to produce a shock wave that caused less collateral damage than the baradium-collapsium mix.

==History==
{{Listen|filename=Seismic charge.flac|title=SeismicCharge.flac|description=An exploding Void-7 seismic charge}}
[[File:Seismic_Charge.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Void-7's shock wave over Geonosis.]]
[[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] installed a Void-7 launcher aboard his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], prior to the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]]. The seismic charges were held in place by magnetic clamps, and released through an airlock situated between the vessel's engines. He deployed a number of seismic charges against [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 interceptor]] over Geonosis, knowing the Void-7's erratic trajectory would be difficult to evade even for a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. However, Kenobi was able to avoid two seismic charges, and both he and Fett ultimately survived their [[Dogfight over Geonosis/Legends|dogfight]].

Some Delta-7 [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] were also fitted with seismic charge launchers during the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] reactivated a Delta-7 on Geonosis that had laid dormant since [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. During the [[Battle of Geonosis (Galactic Civil War)|fight]] to reach an orbital [[Syliure-31 hyperspace docking ring/Legends|hyperspace ring]], Antilles launched seismic charges at pursuing [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Imperial escort carrier (storm commando)|escort carriers]].

==Behind the scenes==
The Void-7 seismic charge first appeared in the [[2002]] ''[[Star Wars]]'' film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]''. ''

In the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]], ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', both ''Slave I'' and Delta-7 Jedi starfighters are equipped with the seismic charges.
